entries.reason: Tenant resolution corrected so a principal resolves its own tenant rather than the platform default, plus an honest session-degradation signal (roadmap 7.1.2 follow-up, both raised in review of PR #421). resolveTenantPrincipalContext passed the hard-coded platform default to resolveBoundTenantPrincipal as the request preferred tenant, but that parameter is a filter and not a ranking, so the helper admitted only the pair (tecpey,main): verified against a migrated database, a principal bound elsewhere resolved to binding_missing and one in a non-default workspace of the default tenant to workspace_mismatch. The filter is load-bearing and is kept for callers that genuinely assert a tenant (assertedTenantId/assertedWorkspaceId) and left null when nothing was asserted, so the existing ORDER BY ranks default-first then oldest binding; a principal still only ever resolves to a binding of its own. Separately, strictRevocationVerdict now distinguishes an unreachable revocation authority from a decision it made, and the GET reports degraded only for the former, so a valid account-only session (which academy-auth signs on every login before profile completion) no longer reports a false outage. The POST handler on this file is unchanged; its sourceHash moves because the file is shared and its testReferences gained certificate-session-degradation-postgres.test.ts. No control was weakened.
